products.title: YL-46 Slant Bed CNC Lathe
products.summary: High-rigidity 30° slant-bed CNC lathe for automated bar-stock production, featuring gang-type tooling, hydraulic clamping, ±0.01 mm accuracy, and a maximum spindle speed of 4,000 rpm.
products.html:
Product Overview

This slant-bed CNC lathe is designed for high-volume production of steel, iron, aluminum, and stainless-steel bar stock up to 35 mm in diameter, as well as automatic bar-fed production of forged parts and other blanks up to 50 mm in diameter. Its high-rigidity, deformation-resistant structure incorporates multiple patented technologies and is suitable for components requiring a single-side cutting allowance of up to 2 mm, dimensional accuracy within ±0.01 mm, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6.

It is an ideal automation upgrade for flat-bed CNC lathes, cam-type automatic lathes, and hydraulic lathes, helping reduce labor costs while improving production consistency and product quality.

posts.title: What to Include in a CNC Machine RFQ: A Workpiece-First Checklist
posts.html:
A useful CNC machine request for quotation (RFQ) starts with the workpiece, the required process and the production target. A machine name alone does not tell a supplier how the part will be located, which operations must share a setup or how output will be measured. For valve, sanitary-ware and hardware manufacturers, a complete brief helps suppliers compare a standard machine, a multi-spindle configuration and a custom solution against the same requirement. Use the checklist below to prepare that brief and identify the points that still need technical review.

1. Identify the workpiece and drawing revision

Attach the latest controlled drawing and identify its revision. Include a 3D model where available, along with clear photographs of the blank and finished part. Mark features that are difficult to understand from a single view, including cross holes, internal passages, threads and areas with restricted tool access.

If you supply several similar parts, show the complete part family. A machine that suits one reference part may need different fixtures, tools or travel for another. Label each file with the part number and revision so that suppliers do not base their proposals on different versions.

  • Part number, drawing revision and units.
  • Overall dimensions, weight and loading orientation.
  • Blank and finished-part photographs.
  • Available locating surfaces and clamping restrictions.
  • Related parts and the differences between them.

2. Specify material and blank condition

State the material grade rather than only writing “brass,” “steel” or “aluminum.” Explain whether the incoming part is a casting, forging, bar-stock blank or partially machined component. Where relevant, include hardness, surface condition, machining allowance and the variation expected between blanks.

These details influence cutting tools, workholding and the proposed process. If the material or allowance is not yet fixed, record the alternatives and ask the supplier to state which one the quotation assumes.

3. List the complete process, not just the main operation

Break the job into drilling, tapping, milling, boring, chamfering, turning, deburring and inspection steps as applicable. Identify the faces that require machining, which operations must share a datum and which features are already finished before the part reaches the machine.

For an illustrative brass angle-valve body inquiry, the brief might include the blank drawing, hole locations, thread standards, sealing surfaces and the permitted clamping areas. It should also say whether burr removal, washing or leak testing belongs in the equipment scope. This example describes the information to provide; it does not establish a machine configuration or guaranteed result.

A product such as Yueli’s dual-spindle drilling, tapping and milling compound machine is one route to evaluate when several operations can be combined. Its suitability still depends on the drawing, fixture, tooling and required process.

4. Define tolerances and inspection methods

Highlight the dimensions that determine acceptance. Include hole diameter, thread type and effective depth, positional requirements, surface finish and any relationship between features machined in different orientations.

State how each critical feature will be inspected. A dimensional tolerance, a thread-gauge requirement and a functional leak test are different acceptance conditions. For threads, specify the standard, size, pitch, tolerance class and gauge requirement rather than only the nominal diameter.

Ask suppliers to explain the proposed machine, fixture and inspection approach for the critical features. Do not treat an advertised machine accuracy as a guarantee for every finished workpiece.

5. Separate cycle time from required production output

Provide the required good parts per hour or shift, working hours, expected batch size and frequency of model changes. If you already have a cycle-time target, explain what it includes.

A useful cycle definition accounts for loading, locating, clamping, tool approach, machining, indexing, retracting, unloading and any in-cycle inspection. Also identify whether the quoted output assumes one part or several parts per cycle.

  • Required good parts per hour or shift.
  • Available shifts and working hours.
  • Annual volume and typical batch size.
  • Number of operators and their assigned tasks.
  • Changeover frequency and acceptable setup time.
  • Any allowance for inspection, tool changes and planned stops.

Keep estimated output separate from trial-proven output. A quotation should identify the assumptions that a workpiece trial or factory acceptance test will need to verify.

6. Describe loading, fixtures and automation boundaries

Explain whether loading will be manual, semi-automatic or automatic. If the machine must connect to a bar feeder, robot, conveyor, assembly station or test system, define the interface and who supplies each item.

For fixtures, identify the intended locating datum, accessible clamping surfaces, permitted contact marks and product-change requirements. Ask whether tooling, gauges, fixture sets and change parts are included in the offer.

When a standard configuration cannot cover the process, the same workpiece brief supports a special-purpose machine and custom equipment review. Define the required outcome before specifying a particular mechanism.

7. Provide destination and installation conditions

Include the destination country, factory power supply, frequency, phase arrangement and available compressed-air conditions. Provide the installation space, access route and any restrictions on machine dimensions or handling.

List the documentation, language, installation, training and service support your team needs. If the project has destination-specific conformity requirements, state them for review against the exact machine and configuration. Confirm the applicable documentation during the technical discussion.

Yueli’s equipment quotation, delivery and service FAQ provides the current general information. The final offer should specify the terms and inclusions for your order.

8. Agree on trial and FAT acceptance criteria

Define how the proposed equipment will be evaluated before shipment. Factory acceptance testing (FAT) should use an agreed drawing revision, sample material, tooling and test method.

  • Workpiece sample quantity and supply responsibility.
  • Critical dimensions, gauges and inspection records.
  • Cycle-time start and finish points.
  • Trial duration and acceptable operating conditions.
  • Required functions, interfaces and safety checks.
  • Manuals, electrical drawings, backup files and spare-parts lists.
  • Witnessing arrangements and the process for resolving open items.

Do not postpone acceptance criteria until the machine is finished. Including them in the RFQ lets each supplier account for the same verification work.

9. Copy this CNC machine RFQ checklist

Use the fields below in an email or procurement document. Mark incomplete items “To be confirmed during technical review” instead of leaving suppliers to guess.

10. Compare quotations against the same brief

Review the technical scope before comparing the price. Ask each supplier to distinguish the base machine, options, fixtures, tooling, automation interfaces, inspection equipment, installation and training. Record exclusions and responsibilities explicitly.

You can use the Yueli equipment catalog to identify reference machines. If you still need to decide between equipment routes, read the workpiece-first drilling, tapping and milling machine selection guide before finalizing the RFQ.

Keep a list of open points alongside each quotation. Price, lead time and output remain difficult to compare when one offer includes a complete fixture and another assumes the buyer will supply it.

Frequently asked questions

Can I request a quotation without a finished drawing?

You can begin with photographs, a sample description, material, approximate dimensions and the required process. Treat the response as an initial discussion. A firm technical scope may need a controlled drawing, physical sample or further measurements.

Should I specify the machine model in the RFQ?

Include a reference model if you have one, but attach the workpiece requirements as well. Ask the supplier to identify any configuration changes or limitations rather than assuming that the reference machine covers the complete job.

Which information is most useful for an initial Yueli inquiry?

Start with five items: a workpiece drawing or sample photo, material and key dimensions, required process and tolerance, target output, and destination country. Add the detailed RFQ fields as the project develops.

Send your workpiece for an equipment discussion

Prepare the available drawing or photos, material, required operations and production target. Start through the contact page and describe the files you have; if a file-upload option is unavailable, ask the team how to send the drawing for review.

posts.title: How to Choose a Drilling, Tapping and Milling Machine: A Workpiece-First Checklist
posts.html:
Short answer: choose a drilling, tapping and milling machine from the workpiece and process route—not from a model name alone. The right starting data are the part drawing, material, hole and thread details, tolerance, target output, loading method and available floor space. With those facts, a supplier can compare a dedicated tapping machine, a compound machine and a CNC machining center against the same production requirement.


This guide gives manufacturing engineers and sourcing teams a practical way to prepare that comparison before requesting a quotation.


Start with the workpiece, not the machine


A useful equipment inquiry describes what must be produced and how success will be measured. Before comparing machines, collect:



  • the latest workpiece drawing or clear photos;

  • material and current blank condition;

  • overall dimensions, clamping surfaces and datum strategy;

  • hole diameters, thread sizes, depths and positional requirements;

  • all required processes, including drilling, tapping, milling, chamfering or boring;

  • critical tolerances and inspection method;

  • target pieces per hour or required cycle time;

  • annual volume, batch size and expected model changeovers;

  • manual, semi-automatic or automatic loading expectations;

  • destination country, power supply and available installation space.


If these inputs are incomplete, two suppliers may quote very different machines because they are solving different versions of the job. A clear technical brief makes price, capacity and risk comparisons more meaningful.


Match the process route to the machine type










Machine routeBest fitQuestions to check
Dedicated drilling or tapping machineStable parts with a limited process sequence and straightforward fixturesCan one spindle and one setup meet the required output and thread quality?
Compound drilling, tapping and milling machineParts that benefit from combining operations or parallel spindle workDo spindle spacing, travel, tooling and clamping match the drawing?
CNC drilling and tapping centerMore program variation, tool changes or geometry flexibilityAre axis travel, tool capacity, spindle characteristics and control functions sufficient?
Multi-spindle or custom automationHigh-volume production where cycle time, loading and process balance dominateIs the projected volume stable enough to justify dedicated tooling and automation?

Browse Yueli’s drilling, tapping and milling equipment, tapping machines and CNC machining centers to see the main equipment routes before narrowing the configuration.


Seven checkpoints for a defensible machine comparison


1. Confirm the processing envelope


Check every relevant dimension against the proposed configuration: axis travel, distance from spindle to table, fixture height, tool approach, clearance for clamps and safe chip evacuation. Nominal part dimensions alone are not enough because the fixture, toolholder and loading motion also consume space.


2. Separate spindle speed from usable cutting performance


Maximum spindle speed is only one input. Material, tool diameter, thread size, cutting method, torque and duty cycle determine whether the spindle is suitable. Ask the supplier to explain the proposed cutting data and tool choice for your part instead of comparing a single rpm number.


3. Review drilling and tapping depth carefully


Through holes, blind holes and deep holes create different chip-control and tool-life demands. For tapping, identify the thread standard, pitch, effective depth and whether rigid tapping is required. If several hole types share one setup, the tool sequence and cycle balance should be reviewed together.


4. Evaluate process combination and spindle arrangement


A compound machine can reduce handling when drilling, tapping and milling can be completed in one fixture. A dual-spindle layout may also improve process balance for a suitable part. For example, Yueli’s Dual Spindles Drilling, Tapping and Milling Compound Machine lists a 320 mm X-axis screw travel, NT30 spindle taper, 115 mm drilling and tapping stroke, 120 mm spindle spacing and a 32 mm maximum processing diameter in the published catalog data. These values are useful screening inputs, but final suitability still depends on the drawing, fixture and required operations.


5. Compare cycle time as a complete system


Cycle time should include loading, clamping, tool approach, cutting, retracting, indexing, unloading and any inspection step. A fast cutting cycle can still deliver poor output if manual handling or chip clearing becomes the bottleneck. Ask for the assumptions behind a cycle estimate and identify which items must be proven in a workpiece trial.


6. Plan for changeover, tooling and maintenance


High-mix production often values repeatable setup and program flexibility more than the absolute shortest cycle. Review fixture change time, tool access, parameter storage, operator skill requirements and access for routine maintenance. For ongoing care, see the guide to drilling and tapping machine maintenance.


7. Define acceptance criteria before ordering


Agree on how the machine will be evaluated. Typical acceptance items include processed sample dimensions, thread gauges, surface requirements, cycle-time conditions, continuous-run duration, safety checks, included tooling and the documentation supplied with the machine. Measurable acceptance criteria protect both buyer and supplier from ambiguous expectations.


A practical request-for-quotation checklist


Send the following information in one package:



  1. workpiece drawing, 3D file if available, and photos;

  2. material specification and blank condition;

  3. process list with critical dimensions and tolerances;

  4. current process route and known production problems;

  5. target output, working hours and batch pattern;

  6. loading, unloading and automation preference;

  7. inspection requirements and acceptance method;

  8. factory power, air supply, floor-space and destination details;

  9. requested delivery window, training and after-sales expectations.


You can compare available models in the Yueli equipment catalog. If the application does not fit a standard model, provide the same technical package for a custom automation review.


Frequently asked questions


When should I choose a compound machine instead of separate machines?


A compound machine is worth evaluating when several operations can share one stable fixture and reduced handling improves consistency or throughput. Separate machines may remain preferable when processes require very different setups, the production mix changes frequently or independent capacity is more valuable.


When is a CNC drilling and tapping center the better choice?


A CNC center is often a stronger candidate when the part family needs programmed position changes, multiple tools, broader geometry flexibility or frequent model changeover. Confirm the travel, spindle, tool system, control functions and fixture envelope against the full part family.


What information is needed for an accurate quotation?


At minimum, provide the drawing or photos, material, dimensions, process and tolerance requirements, target output, loading preference and destination country. A quotation made without this information should be treated as preliminary.


Can one machine process copper, zinc alloy and steel?


Potentially, but material changes affect tooling, cutting data, coolant, chip handling and sometimes spindle requirements. Compatibility should be confirmed for the exact part and production target rather than assumed from a general material list.


How should I compare suppliers’ cycle-time claims?


Ask each supplier to state the same boundaries: loading, clamping, cutting, tool changes, unloading and inspection. Then identify which assumptions will be verified during a sample run or acceptance test.


Next step: request a workpiece-based review


Yueli Automation develops standard equipment and custom production solutions around the workpiece and required process. Review the company and manufacturing capabilities, then send your drawing and production requirements for a focused equipment discussion.

Frequently Asked Questions

Find answers to common questions about our CNC machining equipment, custom automation solutions, shipping, and after-sales support. If you need further technical assistance, our engineering team is always ready to help.


Can you customize automation equipment for specific production lines?


Yes, absolutely. Since 2013, we have specialized in providing tailored CNC machining and automation solutions. Our engineering team will evaluate your product drawings and processing requirements to design equipment that perfectly matches your sanitary ware, valve, or industrial component manufacturing needs.



What materials and industries are your machines suitable for?


Our equipment is widely used in the sanitary ware, plumbing, valve, and general hardware industries. The machines are designed for high-precision cutting, drilling, and processing of various metal materials, including brass, copper, stainless steel, aluminum, and zinc alloys.



What is the typical lead time for your machinery?


For our standard CNC machines, the lead time is typically 30 to 45 days. For fully customized automation lines, the design, manufacturing, and comprehensive testing process usually takes 60 to 90 days, depending on the complexity of your specific project.



What kind of after-sales support and warranty do you provide?


We provide a standard 12-month warranty for all our automation equipment. Beyond the warranty period, we offer lifetime technical support. Our dedicated after-sales team is available via video calls, email, and WhatsApp to help troubleshoot issues and ensure your production line runs without extended downtime.



Do you offer overseas installation and operator training?


Yes, we do. Along with detailed English operation manuals and video tutorials, we can dispatch our senior engineers to your factory for on-site installation, commissioning, and staff training for large-scale automation projects (travel and accommodation expenses to be negotiated).



How do I start a project or request a quote from Yueli?


You can easily start by clicking the “Inquire Now” button or contacting us directly via Email or WhatsApp. Please provide your product drawings, material details, and expected daily production capacity. Our sales engineers will review your needs and provide a detailed technical proposal and quotation within 24 hours.

Ready to Upgrade Your Production Line?

Send us your product drawings and processing requirements today. Our senior engineers will provide a customized CNC machining or automation solution and a detailed quote within 24 hours.

01 · Equipment selection

Choosing the Right Equipment

How do I choose the right Yueli equipment?
Start with your workpiece drawing or sample photo. Include the material, key dimensions, required operation, tolerance, target output and destination country. Yueli will review the process before recommending a standard machine or a customized route. You can first browse our equipment families or send the details through the Contact page.
Do you supply both standard and custom equipment?
Yes. A standard machine is suitable when a published configuration meets the part and process requirements. Customized equipment or integration is considered when special tooling, fixtures, multiple operations, automation or inspection functions are required.
02 · Application review

Workpiece, Material & Process

Which industries do you serve?
Yueli serves a range of machining and automation applications. Current focus industries include sanitary ware, fire protection valves, door-control hardware, electrical hardware, aerospace and machinery manufacturing.
What information is needed for a technical review?
Please provide five core items: a workpiece drawing or sample photo; material and key dimensions; required process and tolerance; target output or cycle requirement; and destination country. Clear information helps reduce quotation revisions.
03 · Engineering scope

Customization and Technical Review

Can the equipment be customized?
Yes, after a technical review. The confirmed scope may include machine configuration, tooling, fixtures, accessories, automation integration, inspection or testing functions. Final feasibility depends on the workpiece and process requirements.
How is the technical proposal prepared?
Yueli first reviews the part and process. The team then defines the machine scope, confirms interfaces and testing requirements, and prepares the technical and commercial proposal. Unconfirmed precision or performance figures are not treated as final specifications.
04 · Commercial terms

Quotation and Payment

How long is a quotation valid?
A quotation is generally valid for 15 days. If the validity period has expired, please ask Yueli to reconfirm pricing, component availability and delivery conditions before placing the order.
Which payment methods are available?
T/T and L/C are available. The final payment schedule and documentary requirements are confirmed in the quotation or sales contract for the specific order.
05 · Production and shipment

Lead Time, FAT and Delivery

What is the typical lead time?
The typical equipment lead time is 10–30 days after the technical and commercial scope is confirmed. Actual timing depends on customization, component availability, tooling, fixtures and the agreed testing plan.
Is factory acceptance testing available?
Testing and inspection can be planned according to the confirmed project scope. Acceptance items and criteria should be agreed during the technical review so both parties understand what will be checked before shipment.
How are machines packed and shipped?
Yueli provides export packing. Please provide the destination country and delivery requirements so the packing and shipping arrangement can be discussed and stated in the order documents.
06 · Service

Installation, Training and Warranty

Do you provide overseas installation and training?
Yes, overseas installation and training are available. Unless included in a written quotation, overseas on-site installation and related travel expenses are not included and will be quoted separately.
What warranty do you provide?
The complete machine warranty is 12 months. Wear parts and consumables are excluded. Human-caused damage is handled separately according to the actual situation and confirmed service terms.
What after-sales support is available?
Yueli provides lifetime online technical guidance. Warranty service follows the confirmed order terms, while parts, consumables and on-site service outside the agreed scope are handled separately.
07 · Inquiry

Starting an Inquiry

How do I start an equipment or automation inquiry?
Send your workpiece and process information by email, WhatsApp or the Contact page. Include the drawing or photo, material and dimensions, required process and tolerance, target output and destination country. Contact nina.h@yueli-tech.com, WhatsApp +86 136 0076 8411, or use the inquiry page.
